A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multispectral demosaicing work and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Corresponding content can be matched despite pagination and figure-number changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original demosaicing experiments, quantitative comparisons, ablations, and supplementary analyses using the proposed RGB-MS dataset.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds a cross-dataset generalization experiment in supplementary Section 8.1.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 changes the stated fusion-network backbone from Restormer to NAFNet. The two-stage procedure, spectral alignment layer, optical-flow alignment, and losses remain unchanged. The PDFs do not explain whether the backbone revision reflects an implementation change or a correction.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates within the authors' controlled RGB-MS acquisition dataset. v3 adds evaluation using the independent HS dataset [27], containing 60 HS-HS pairs projected into MS/RGB mosaics. This substantially extends coverage beyond the original acquisition domain; the existing demosaicing and reconstruction tasks remain.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged. The new generalization experiment reuses MCAN and HSIFN, already evaluated in v1. Additional alignment descriptions for DCT and HSIFN do not establish that their implementations changed.

E3.justification: The added generalization experiment introduces testing on externally sourced HS images projected through the authors' MSFA/CFA responses, with the proposed model trained solely on the original dataset. Existing splits, training budgets, patch sizes, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Supplementary Section 8.1 and Figure 10 add a focused cross-dataset generalization test with quantitative and qualitative evidence. Existing RGB-guidance ablations, SAL attribution analysis, optical-flow visualizations, and RGB/MS reconstruction analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing Diffusion Index averaging over 206 sampled regions is unchanged, and the new generalization results add no uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 newly reports cross-dataset PSNR of 42.48 dB for MCAN+Ours, 39.40 dB for MCAN, and 40.27 dB for HSIFN, alongside Figure 10. Existing quantitative tables and qualitative result panels retain their values. These are additional results under new conditions, not same-setting performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: Equations 1–17 retain the same mathematical content, including fusion, losses, image formation, noise modeling, and color calibration. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: RGB-guided MS demosaicing, the paired RGB-MS dataset, and state-of-the-art reconstruction claims. The added appendix evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new results as evidence of generalization while acknowledging discrepancies from HS precision, spectral calibration, sensor nonlinearities, and noise. Section 9.1 also adds a mechanism comparison with HSIFN involving attention placement and deformable alignment. The original limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds code/data access information, explicitly states that baselines are retrained from scratch with matching training configurations and iteration counts, and documents DCT/HSIFN alignment adaptations. These are newly disclosed details, not demonstrated experimental reruns. The earlier paragraph explaining construction of larger '-L' variants is removed.

R1.justification: The cited-work inventory remains unchanged, but supplementary Section 9.1 adds substantive positioning against HSIFN, distinguishing fusion strategy, alignment, and computational cost. The main related-work discussion is otherwise retained.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized wording, author-name, typo, and cross-reference corrections. It inserts a Generalization subsection and revises the architecture-details section into additional experimental details and discussion, without extensively rewriting the paper.

P2.justification: v3 adds generalization Figure 10, renumbers subsequent figures, relocates existing appendix tables, and adjusts figure/table spacing. The limitations paragraph now fits on main-text page 8. Existing qualitative panels are preserved rather than replaced.

improvement.justification: The independent-dataset test in Section 8.1 adds useful evidence beyond v1's single acquisition domain, while baseline preparation details and code/data access information improve reproducibility. The gains are limited: the new test uses simulated mosaics, existing results remain unchanged, and the fusion-backbone revision is unexplained.
